steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Some Christians read Genesis literally (creationist view) while others read it as symbolic or metaphorical, compatible with scientific theories like the Big Bang and evolution.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Creation
steps.body: 1. For Creation questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Creation to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain two different Christian beliefs about creation. | Q: How does John 1:1-3 contribute to Christian understanding of creation?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
